hunt.justification: Legitimate MDM platforms provide a trusted, privileged path for software deployment that bypasses most endpoint security alerts. A negative result confirming no unauthorized enrollments is a high-value security assurance.

related.reason: A broader hunt for RMM tools that does not focus on the MDM delivery vector.

meta.analysis: This is a hunt because detection rules for legitimate software like Rippling or ScreenConnect often trigger excessive noise. This hunt correlates the social engineering lure (DNS), the enrollment (rare registry keys), and the C2 activity (relay traffic) into a single phased attack chain triage.

scenario.summary: Attackers leverage business-themed phishing lures to trick users into installing or enrolling in rogue MDM platforms like Hexnode and Rippling. Once enrolled, the attackers use the MDM's administrative privileges to deploy ScreenConnect RMM agents, providing persistent remote access to the compromised endpoints.

meta.rationale: Start by identifying all hosts with Rippling or Hexnode agents. In many environments, these will be absent, making any hit suspicious. Focus on endpoints where users might be lured by business proposals or meeting invites.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker uses social engineering to enroll a device into an unauthorized MDM tenant, providing a persistent and privileged path to deploy a rogue RMM tool for remote access.

hunt.name: Rogue MDM and RMM Deployment
hunt.description: This hunt examines the abuse of legitimate Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms like Hexnode and Rippling. Attackers use business-themed phishing lures, such as fake DocuSign installers or Teams meeting invitations, to facilitate enrollment. Once enrolled, the MDM platform is used to deploy ScreenConnect agents that connect to attacker-controlled relays. The hunt follows a phased flow: first identifying MDM software presence and suspicious enrollment registry keys, then searching for the phishing lure execution and outbound RMM network traffic on non-standard ports. This correlation across identity, registry, and network telemetry distinguishes malicious use of these tools from legitimate administration.

nodes.label: Identify hosts with target MDM software

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%rippling%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%hexnode%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%rippling%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%hexnode%'
config.description: Scope the investigation to hosts running Hexnode or Rippling software, which are the platforms observed in this campaign.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames with MDM software. Silence means these platforms are not present in the estate.

primitive_config.label: Identify hosts with target MDM software
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%rippling%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%hexnode%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%rippling%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%hexnode%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames with MDM software. Silence means these platforms are not present in the estate.

nodes.label: DNS queries for phishing lure domains

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{phishing_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Match host activity against the lookalike Teams and DocuSign domains used to deliver the MDM installers.
config.expected_signal: Any resolution of these domains by a scoped host. Silence may mean the attacker used different domains or the logs have expired.

primitive_config.label: DNS queries for phishing lure domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{phishing_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Any resolution of these domains by a scoped host. Silence may mean the attacker used different domains or the logs have expired.

config.content: SELECT reg_key_path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE (LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%rippling%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%hexnode%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY reg_key_path HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Find rare MDM enrollment keys that stand out from the normal management baseline of the fleet.
config.expected_signal: Rippling or Hexnode keys appearing on only a few hosts, which is suspicious in an estate that does not use them for primary management.

primitive_config.label: Stack-count rare MDM enrollment keys
primitive_config.content: SELECT reg_key_path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE (LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%rippling%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%hexnode%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY reg_key_path HAVING host_count <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Rippling or Hexnode keys appearing on only a few hosts, which is suspicious in an estate that does not use them for primary management.

config.objective: Identify hosts that resolved phishing domains and subsequently showed rare MDM-related registry modifications.
config.description: Analyze whether the inventory, DNS lookups, and rare registry keys suggest an unauthorized MDM enrollment.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts showing evidence of phishing interaction followed by MDM presence.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of suspicious if the DNS and registry signals align.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_name, file_path, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{lure_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(file_name) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find host evidence of the specific installer files named in the research using the lure_keywords list.
config.expected_signal: File create or open events for the phishing lure installers. Any row is a high-confidence match for the delivery stage.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_hostname, dst_endpoint_port, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND (dst_endpoint_port = 8041 OR instr(',' || '{{rmm_relays}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify outbound connections to the reported ScreenConnect relays or the common relay port 8041.
config.expected_signal: Outbound traffic identifying the RMM command-and-control stage. Silence means the relays have rotated or the tool is dormant.

config.objective: Determine if any host shows the complete sequence from phishing lure execution to rogue MDM enrollment and RMM C2 communication.
config.description: Decide whether the combined evidence from early enrollment and follow-on RMM activity indicates a confirmed intrusion.
config.expected_signal: A detailed per-host assessment citing the alignment of phishing, enrollment, and RMM traffic.
config.success_criteria: A final verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign per host.

config.question: the final-attack-chain-triage verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the final-attack-chain-triage verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Direct the hunt based on the agent's confidence in the maliciousness of the chain.
Sever the attacker's RMM and MDM connection by isolating the compromised host.
config.instructions: Isolate the host immediately. After isolation, remove the unauthorized MDM management profile and uninstall any rogue ScreenConnect agents.

config.description: Review the agent's findings and confirm whether the MDM enrollment was truly unauthorized.
config.instructions: Verify the cited rows from the final triage. Check internal IT documentation to see if Rippling or Hexnode was recently adopted or used by a specific department. If not authorized, proceed with incident response.

config.description: Record the results and update the baseline for future hunts.
config.instructions: Log the examined hosts. If any were found to be legitimately running these MDM tools, update the authorized software inventory to prevent future false positives.
